### `epx agent roles`

Usage: `epx agent roles [status] [--json]; epx agent roles set <role> <model> [--effort <level>] [--json]; epx agent roles suggest [--model <id>] [--apply] [--json]`

omo (Codex / LazyCodex): show each Codex agent role's model pin, set one role's model in its TOML and in omo.jsonc, or suggest a model for every role.

State-changing: yes. JSON mode: `payload`.

| Method | Route |
|---|---|
| GET | `/api/codex-agent-roles` |
| PUT | `/api/codex-agent-roles/{role}` |
| POST | `/api/codex-agent-roles/auto-assign` |

| Flag | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | boolean | Emit the role list, the write result or the proposals as JSON. |
| `--effort` | string | set: also write the role's reasoning effort. |
| `--model` | string | suggest: size the roles with this model instead of the Codex default model. |
| `--apply` | boolean | suggest: write every proposal through the role model write. |

- A bare invocation reads and never writes.
- Requires Codex-based omo (LazyCodex): the omo@sisyphuslabs Codex plugin enabled in config.toml and installed; otherwise status lists no roles, and set and suggest are refused.
- set rewrites only the root model value of $CODEX_HOME/agents/<role>.toml, plus model_reasoning_effort with --effort; omo.jsonc gets the same model and, when LazyCodex has that level, the effort as reasoning; it is skipped when absent or when it contains comments.
- suggest sizes every role with one model call and prints proposals without writing; --apply writes each proposed model and effort.

- Requires daemon support for experimental thread/queue/add. Sender context comes from CODEX_THREAD_ID, not an authentication claim.
- queued means submitted, not processed. unknown must not be replayed; no automatic retry, daemon start or thread resume.
- Exit 0: queued; 1: not sent; 3: unknown; 64: invalid usage. No Claude transport, native lifecycle mutation or skill installation.

### `epx message mcp`

Usage: `epx message mcp --codex <absolute-cli-path> --codex-home <absolute-existing-home> [--allow-reply-read] [--allow-resume --resume-socket <absolute-existing-unix-socket> --resume-permissions <profile-id>]`

Serve MCP tools for stored Codex metadata, queued text, opt-in stored-turn reply reads, bounded waits and guarded existing-server resume preflight.

State-changing: yes. JSON mode: `none`.

Drives no management route.

| Flag | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--codex` | string | Explicit local Codex CLI executable. |
| `--codex-home` | string | Explicit existing Codex home; no creation or login. |
| `--allow-reply-read` | boolean | Explicitly expose stored final-turn text through codex_read_reply and codex_wait_reply; disabled by default. |
| `--allow-resume` | boolean | Expose existing-thread resume preflight; requires --resume-socket and --resume-permissions. Execution is blocked pending native atomic resume support. |
| `--resume-socket` | string | Existing trusted local Unix App Server socket; requires --allow-resume, --resume-permissions and matching Codex home. |
| `--resume-permissions` | string | Host-selected native profile for resume preflight; does not bypass the atomicity refusal or preserve saved permissions automatically. |

- macOS/Linux only. Default queue/read tools need no proxy/control socket; resume uses the explicitly configured existing Unix socket. Starts bounded stdio helpers only when a tool is called; existing sessions/send behavior stays unchanged.
- Stored threads are not verified live sessions. queued is not processing; unknown is never replayed. --allow-reply-read exposes bounded same-turn final text, not exclusive reply ownership or goal completion. No daemon start, steer, automatic replies or registration. Resume preflight is separate opt-in through a same-home existing Unix server; managed requirements and unavailable profiles refuse. The checked native API cannot enforce unloaded-only resume atomically, so execution is blocked with resume_atomicity_unsupported; no thread/resume is sent.

### `epx advisor`

Inspect and configure the advisor sidecar (expert consultation for routed workers).

State-changing: yes. JSON mode: `payload`.

| Method | Route |
|---|---|
| GET | `/api/advisor/settings` |
| GET | `/api/advisor/activity` |
| PUT | `/api/advisor/settings` |

| Flag | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | boolean | Emit advisor settings as JSON. |
| `--context-mode` | string | With set: context (default) or question-only; question-only pauses automatic consultations. |

- `status` (the default) reads the resolved settings; `on`/`off` toggle the sidecar; `consent` records or revokes context-sharing consent; `set` updates model, effort, policy, context mode, task limit, or timeout.
- `on` does not grant consent. Without current consent it refuses and prints the disclosure. `on --ack-context-sharing` records consent v1 and enables. `consent --revoke` removes consent: consultations not yet dispatched are blocked, but it cannot cancel a dispatched consultation or retract task context already sent.
- The advisor model may be any routable model string: a bare native model, an explicit `provider/model`, or an account-qualified native model.
- `policy: preflight` makes EasyProxy attempt one automatic consultation per task with a stable conversation identity once the task shows orientation evidence (an assistant tool call or a tool result after the latest user message). Without a stable identity, each eligible request may trigger another consultation. `policy: manual` consults only when the worker calls the synthetic `advisor` tool. Neither path sends task context without current context-sharing consent.
- `policy: adaptive` adds evidence-based failed-repair consultation after the same validation fails, a file edit completes, and validation fails again. Automatic calls require a stable conversation identity. `set --max-consultations <1-3>` caps adaptive task attempts, including manual calls, in a durable 24-hour budget. No semantic stuck detection is claimed.
- `set --context-mode question-only` sends only a fixed instruction and a required, self-contained worker question (up to 2,000 retained characters plus a truncation notice). No task history, tools, worker identity or repair evidence is attached. Automatic preflight and adaptive repair calls are paused; manual calls, consent and existing limits still apply. `set --context-mode context` restores the default context-sharing behavior and selected policy.
- `activity` reads up to 100 recent consultation metadata records (trigger, status, models, requested and mapped effort, duration, reported tokens); no task or advice content is retained. Records are process-local and expire after 24 hours. Missing mapped effort means unreported, not successful application.

### `epx v2 status`

Usage: `epx v2 [status] [--live] [--json]`

Report local multi-agent mode and Codex feature settings.

State-changing: no. JSON mode: `envelope`.

| Method | Route |
|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v2` |

| Flag | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--live` | boolean | Use the selected runtime; otherwise preserve the local native/config operation. |
| `--json` | boolean | Emit the validated task result as one JSON document. |

- Local and live targets never fall back into each other. Parse failures occur before native effects; JSON is one safe state/change/sync result, not collected log text.
- Local mode/keep-native and changed on/off preserve their existing sync calls even without a discovered port; threads/hints and unchanged toggles do not gain sync. Unknown or failed sync evidence is nonzero with landed state visible.
- Live writes use actual post-write state and full catalog outcomes; a502 can mean partial native changes. Read back before retrying; no rollback is implied.

### `epx combo set`

Usage: `epx combo set <id> [--targets <provider/model[:weight],...> | --targets-file <FILE|->] [--strategy <failover|round-robin|random|least-used|reset-window|jev|ewma-latency>] [--sticky <1-100|->] [--ewma-alpha <0.01-1|->] [--ewma-half-life-ms <1000-3600000|->] [--ewma-min-samples <1-20|->] [--ewma-error-penalty-ms <100-600000|->] [--cooldown-reprobe <on|off>] [--cooldown-reprobe-interval <ms>] [--effort <low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultra|->] [--effort-mode <fallback|force|->] [--alias <name|->] [--native-alias [on|off]] [--allow-metered-targets <on|off>] [--display-name <label|->] [--description <text|->] [--decision-provider <provider|-> | --decision-model <route|->] [--decision-timeout <ms|->] [--decision-quota-signals <on|off|->] [--decision-quota-tiers <JSON|->] [--session-pin <duration|->] [--session-pin-effort <pinned|per-turn>] [--rename-from <id>] [--image-input <auto|disabled>] [--reasoning-effort-mode <strict|adaptive>] [--jev-effort-mode <decide|client>] [--json]`

Create, update or rename a combo.

State-changing: yes. JSON mode: `payload`.

| Method | Route |
|---|---|
| GET | `/api/combos` |
| PUT | `/api/combos` |

| Flag | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--allow-metered-targets` | string | on grants operator consent to metered targets only on a loopback-only proxy; off clears it. |
| `--targets` | string | Ordered provider/model[:weight] list; required for creation. |
| `--strategy` | string | Routing strategy. |
| `--sticky` | string | Round-robin limit 1-100; - resets. |
| `--ewma-alpha` | number | EWMA smoothing factor in 0.01..1; - resets. |
| `--ewma-half-life-ms` | number | EWMA time-decay half-life 1000..3600000 ms; - clears. |
| `--ewma-min-samples` | number | Cold-start probe samples per target 1..20; - resets. |
| `--ewma-error-penalty-ms` | number | Latency penalty on target failure 100..600000 ms; - resets. |
| `--cooldown-reprobe` | string | Opt into one recovery pass when all eligible targets cool; off by default. |
| `--cooldown-reprobe-interval` | string | Minimum interval between recovery passes in ms (1000..86400000); default 300000. |
| `--effort` | string | Default effort; - clears. |
| `--effort-mode` | string | fallback or force; - resets to fallback. |
| `--alias` | string | Alias; - clears. |
| `--display-name` | string | Label; - clears. |
| `--description` | string | Catalog row description; - clears. |
| `--decision-provider` | string | JEV provider; - clears. |
| `--decision-model` | string | JEV route; - clears; exclusive with provider. |
| `--decision-timeout` | string | JEV deadline 1000-120000 ms; - clears. |
| `--decision-quota-signals` | string | JEV advisory quota on/off; - clears. |
| `--decision-quota-tiers` | string | Partial JSON thresholds; - clears. |
| `--session-pin` | string | JEV session pin idle window 1m-24h (90s, 20m, 1h); - clears. |
| `--session-pin-effort` | string | pinned reuses the pinned effort; per-turn asks JEV for the pinned target's effort each turn. |
| `--rename-from` | string | Existing combo ID to rename. |
| `--json` | boolean | Emit structured JSON. |
| `--native-alias` | string | Bare legacy flag means on; explicit on/off preserves presence, including false. |
| `--targets-file` | string | Bounded ordered target JSON array, exclusive with --targets; preserves effort/profile/last-resort metadata. |
| `--image-input` | string | auto or disabled; explicit auto clears the previous disabled choice. |
| `--reasoning-effort-mode` | string | strict or adaptive, distinct from --effort-mode fallback/force. |
| `--jev-effort-mode` | string | JEV wire-effort owner: decide (default) applies the decision effort; client keeps its target and leaves effort to combo policy. |

- create and update are aliases of set. Existing fields are read before writing; --targets replaces targets. Without --strategy an existing combo keeps its stored strategy and JEV policy; a new combo defaults to failover.
- force overrides valid client effort and may increase cost and latency.
- Only the implemented target grammar is supported; full GUI target metadata and routing-profile writes are separate tasks.
- New file/flag conflicts refuse before transport. Partial edits preserve target metadata; explicit false/default values override server carry. Turning a native alias off may also require clearing its incompatible alias.
- Read/merge/write uses one target and remains an upsert without revision CAS. Saved-but-incomplete catalog outcomes return nonzero with their receipt.

| Flag | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--file` | string | Bounded scenarioRouting JSON file or - for stdin; exclusive with scalar flags. |
| `--enabled` | string | Enable or disable scenario routing (on\|off). |
| `--long-context` | string | Target selector for longContext; - clears. |
| `--think` | string | Target selector for think; - clears. |
| `--background` | string | Target selector for background; - clears. |
| `--web-search` | string | Target selector for webSearch; - clears. |
| `--long-context-threshold` | number | Estimated token threshold 1000..10000000. |
| `--think-budget-threshold` | number | Anthropic thinking budget threshold 1..1000000. |
| `--precedence` | string | Comma-separated priority order across background, longContext, webSearch, think. |
| `--match-models` | string | Optional comma-separated selector allowlist; - clears. |
| `--override-explicit` | string | on/off: allow scenario rules on explicit combo/* or policy/* selectors. |
| `--json` | boolean | Emit structured JSON. |

- Validates all configured scenario route selectors against enabled providers before saving.

### `epx workflow-budget status`

Usage: `epx workflow-budget status [--root <id>] [--limit <n>] [--json]`

Inspect tracked workflow-budget roots and recent refusal or clear events.

| Method | Route |
|---|---|
| GET | `/api/workflow-budget` |

| Flag | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|

| `--json` | boolean | Emit the workflow-budget status payload as JSON. |

- Also accepted without `status` (`epx workflow-budget [--root <id>] [--limit <n>] [--json]`). Reads live process memory for active turns, windowed physical sends, distinct children, and recent events.
- When --root is specified, an untracked root returns root: null alongside HTTP 200.

### `epx workflow-budget clear`

Usage: `epx workflow-budget clear [<root-id>] [--root <id>] [--json]`

Clear windowed workflow-budget send and child counts for one root.

State-changing: yes. JSON mode: `payload`.

| Method | Route |
|---|---|
| POST | `/api/workflow-budget/clear` |

| Flag | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--root` | string | Root identifier to clear (mutually exclusive with positional <root-id>; non-empty, <= 200 chars). |
| `--json` | boolean | Emit the clear receipt as JSON. |

- Accepts either a positional <root-id> or --root <id>, never both; sends { root } and leaves active counts, lifetime sends, and token spend ledgers intact.
- Returns exit 4 when the target root is not tracked (404 unknown_root).

### `epx guardrails dry-run`

Usage: `epx guardrails dry-run (--text <str> | --file <path>) [--secret-mode <off|redact|block>] [--compress <on|off>] [--min-chars <512..500000>] [--head-chars <0..100000>] [--tail-chars <0..100000>] [--strip-ansi <on|off>] [--json]`

Evaluate outbound secret guardrails and tool-output compression on synthetic text without mutating state.

State-changing: no. JSON mode: `payload`.

| Method | Route |
|---|---|
| POST | `/api/gateway-guardrails/dry-run` |

| Flag | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--text` | string | Inline text to evaluate (mutually exclusive with --file; max 65536 chars). |
| `--file` | string | Regular non-symlink UTF-8 file to evaluate (max 262144 bytes, decoded max 65536 chars). |
| `--secret-mode` | string | Override outbound secret guard mode for preview: off \| redact \| block. |
| `--compress` | string | Override tool-output compression toggle: on \| off. |
| `--min-chars` | number | Override minimum length for compression (integer 512..500000). |
| `--head-chars` | number | Override leading preserved characters (integer 0..100000). |
| `--tail-chars` | number | Override trailing preserved characters (integer 0..100000). |
| `--strip-ansi` | string | Override ANSI stripping: on \| off. |
| `--json` | boolean | Emit dry-run findings and preview output as JSON. |

- Rejects symlinks, non-regular files, byte reads above 262144, text above 65536 characters, and serialized bodies above 524288 bytes before sending a request.
- Does not mutate live configuration or outbound hygiene counters.

### `epx route to`

Usage: `epx route to <client> <on|off|inherit> [--device <alias|id|this>] [--accounts <all|none|userId,...>] [--model-names <alias|routed>] [--overwrite-conflict] [--local] [--json]`

Set Home-default or per-device route intent, or opt out locally on a Child.

State-changing: yes. JSON mode: `payload`.

| Method | Route |
|---|---|
| PUT | `/api/route-to` |

| Flag | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--device` | string | Home: alias, id, all or this. Child: this or its own link id only. |
| `--json` | boolean | Emit the epx.route-to/1 status matrix. |
| `--overwrite-conflict` | boolean | Explicitly permit replacing conflicting managed blocks. |
| `--local` | boolean | Child only: opt out with off, or clear the opt-out with inherit. |
| `--accounts` | string | Aside on only: all, none, or comma-separated stable userIds; never u/N slots. |
| `--model-names` | string | Hermes/Command Code on only: alias or routed model names. |

- Clients: codex, claude, claude-desktop, grok and the supported file integrations. Without --device a Home updates its default and materializes itself; all is only for status/sync.
- inherit requires --device unless clearing a Child --local opt-out. Child writes print the exact Home command with the Child link id; --local supports off/inherit only. --overwrite-conflict applies only to on or sync.
- On the Home, codex, claude, grok and claude-desktop follow the Home's own native switches: a Home default or --device home write for them writes that switch (Home inherit sets it to the default).

### `epx route to status`

Usage: `epx route to status [--device <alias|id|all|this>] [--json]`

Read per-device route intent, its source and actual client apply outcomes.

State-changing: no. JSON mode: `payload`.

| Method | Route |
|---|---|
| GET | `/api/route-to` |

| Flag | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--device` | string | Home: alias, id, all or this. Child: this or its own link id only. |
| `--json` | boolean | Emit the epx.route-to/1 status matrix. |

- On a Child this reads local receipts without a Home management relay. Intent and applied state are distinct; null applied means no recorded outcome.
- Sources: builtin, default, device, local (Child opt-out) and native (a Home row governed by the Home's own switch). An outcome recorded for an earlier intent reads stale.
- Intent unresolved appears only for Aside, while the Home's existing Aside profiles have no stable userIds and nothing decided Aside; warnings[] then names the fix (epx route to aside on|off --device home).

### `epx route to sync`

Usage: `epx route to sync [--device <alias|id|all|this>] [--overwrite-conflict] [--json]`

Reapply route intent on selected devices, or locally on a Child.

State-changing: yes. JSON mode: `payload`.

| Method | Route |
|---|---|
| POST | `/api/route-to/sync` |

| Flag | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--device` | string | Home: alias, id, all or this. Child: this or its own link id only. |
| `--overwrite-conflict` | boolean | Explicitly permit replacing conflicting managed blocks. |
| `--json` | boolean | Emit the epx.route-to/1 status matrix. |

- No conflict retry or implicit overwrite. Child sync calls its local materializer and sends no Home management write.
- Home sync never changes the Home's native switches for codex, claude, grok or claude-desktop; it refreshes what each switch says.
- On a Home whose Aside ownership is unresolved, sync applies every other client, leaves Aside unchanged, reports it unresolved and prints the warning; that alone does not fail the sync.
